How can I use the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH automation workflow to troubleshoot SSH connection issues?](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-ssh-errors-automation-workflow)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/articles/ARALtPJTdWSCSK8R_nwno_0Q/using-saw-to-diagnose-common-issues-in-your-aws-environment\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH\",\"context\":\"# `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`\\n\\n**Description**\\n\\nThe `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH` runbook installs the Amazon EC2Rescue\\ntool for Linux, and then uses the EC2Rescue tool to check or attempt to fix common\\nissues that prevent a remote connection to the Linux machine via SSH. Optionally,\\nchanges can be applied offline by stopping and starting the instance, if the user\\nexplicitly allows for offline remediation. By default, the runbook operates in\\nread-only mode.\\n\\nRun this Automation (console)\\n\\nFor information about working with the `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH`\\nrunbook, see this `AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH` troubleshooting topic from\\nAWS Premium Support.\\n\\n**Document type**\\n\\nAutomation\\n\\n**Owner**\\n\\nAmazon\\n\\n**Platforms**\\n\\nLinux\\n\\n**Parameters**\\n\\n* Action\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Valid values: CheckAll | FixAll\\n\\n Default: CheckAll\\n\\n Description: (Required) Specify whether to check for issues without fixing\\n them or to check and automatically fix any discovered issues.\\n* AllowOffline\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Valid values: true | false\\n\\n Default: false\\n\\n Description: (Optional) Fix only - Set it to true if you allow an offline\\n SSH remediation in case the online troubleshooting fails, or the provided\\n instance is not a managed instance. Note: For the offline remediation, SSM\\n Automation stops the instance, and creates an AMI before attempting any\\n operations.\\n* AutomationAssumeRole\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Description: (Optional) The Amazon Resource Name (ARN) of the AWS Identity and Access Management\\n (IAM) role that allows Systems Manager Automation to perform the actions on your\\n behalf. If no role is specified, Systems Manager Automation uses the permissions of\\n the user that starts this runbook.\\n* InstanceId\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Description: (Required) ID of your EC2 instance for Linux.\\n* S3BucketName\\n\\n Type: String\\n\\n Description: (Optional) Offline only - S3 bucket name in your account\\n where you want to upload the troubleshooting logs. To reset the password for an AWS account with **sudo** access, [run ssm-user](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-getting-started-ssm-user-permissions.html#ssm-user-permissions-linux). You can also use the EC2 Serial Console to troubleshoot OS-level issues such as boot issues and network configuration issues.\\n\\nTo use Session Manager, your instance must be a [managed node](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/managed_instances.html) and must meet the [Session Manager prerequisites](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-prerequisites.html). The instance's AWS Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) ping status must be **Online**. Also, the attached AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role must have [AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-managed-policy/latest/reference/AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore.html) permissions.\\n\\nTo update your configuration so that it doesn't block SSH access, complete the following steps:\\n\\n1. [Use the EC2 Serial Console to connect to the instance](https\\n\\n*[truncated \u2014 additional content omitted]*\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-linux-resolve-ssh-connection-errors\"},{\"rank_order\":4,\"title\":\"How do I resolve SSH connection issues to my Amazon EC2 Linux instance?\",\"context\":\"### Run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH runbook\\n\\n**Prerequisites:**\\n\\n* Copy the **instance ID** of the unreachable instance.\\n* Make sure that you have the required AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) permissions. Or, [use the AWS Systems Manager console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/running-simple-automations.html#simple-console) and configure the following settings:\\n\\n* For **Automation document**, choose **AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH**.\\n* Under **Document details**, choose **Default version at runtime** for **Runbook version**.\\n* Under **Input parameters**, enter the unreachable instance's ID for **InstanceID** and **FixAll** for **Action**.\\n\\nFor more information, see [Smart RDP and SSH remediation with AWS Systems Manager Automation API actions](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/smart-rdp-and-ssh-remediation-with-aws-systems-manager-automation-api-actions/)\",\"url\":\"https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/ec2-linux-ssh-troubleshooting\"},{\"rank_order\":5,\"title\":\"Reset passwords and SSH keys on EC2 instances\",\"context\":\"## How it works\\n\\nTroubleshooting an instance with Automation and the\\n`AWSSupport-ResetAccess` runbook works as follows:\\n\\n* You specify the ID of the instance and run the runbook.\\n* The system creates a temporary VPC by deploying the\\n EC2Rescue CloudFormation stack.\\n* The system identifies a subnet for your temporary VPC in the same\\n Availability Zone as your original instance.\\n* The system launches a temporary, SSM-enabled helper\\n instance.\\n* The system stops your original instance, and creates a backup. It\\n then attaches the original root volume to the helper\\n instance.\\n* The system uses Run Command to run EC2Rescue on the helper instance.\\n On Windows, EC2Rescue enables password generation for the local\\n Administrator by using EC2Config or EC2Launch on the attached,\\n original root volume. On Linux, EC2Rescue generates and injects a\\n new SSH key and saves the private key, encrypted, in Parameter Store. When\\n finished, EC2Rescue reattaches the root volume back to the original\\n instance.\\n* The system creates a new Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of your instance, now\\n that password generation is enabled. You can use this AMI to\\n create a new EC2 instance, and associate a new key pair if\\n needed.\\n* The system restarts your original instance, and terminates the\\n temporary instance. The system also terminates the temporary VPC and\\n deletes the EC2Rescue CloudFormation stack created at the start of the\\n automation.\\n* **Windows**: Your instance generates\\n a new password you can decode from the Amazon EC2 console using the\\n current key pair assigned to the instance.\\n\\n **Linux**: You can SSH to the\\n instance by using the SSH key stored in Systems Manager Parameter Store as\\n **/ec2rl/openssh/`instance\\n ID`/key**\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/automation-ec2reset.html\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Search AWS docs for SSH troubleshooting runbooks"}

{"id": "58a6f931-8223-4988-b320-028208ad5bfb", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "Yes. **AWSSupport-TroubleshootSSH** is the runbook for this. It's active in us-east-1 in your account (Amazon-owned, version 5).

**What it does**
- It installs the EC2Rescue tool for Linux and checks for the common causes of SSH failures. These include sshd configuration, the sshd service, key and permission problems, and OS firewall rules.
- It works whether or not SSM Agent is running on the instance.
- It runs read-only by default.

**Key parameters**
- `InstanceId` (required): the unreachable instance.
